I held a grudge because they dropped campaign, and co-op campaign is the best part of Tom Clancy games, but it ended up being a well polished multiplayer and co-op experience that offers a good tactical shooter with some interesting gameplay mechanics. My favorite aspects are the ability to destroy parts of the level to open up new sight lines or distract an enemy, coordinate breaches with your team to sweep a room, and that each operator has their own unique ability, none of them overpowered or unbalanced. It's a different kind of shooter than Call of Duty because in Siege, 90% of the fight is won before you even see your enemy; chances are good that one of you already knew the other one was there, and if it isn't you then you're probably about to die.
